name: Validating Manufacturing AI
blurb: Credibility and validation for AI that supports quality decisions.
title: Validating Manufacturing AI
answer: When an AI model supports a quality decision, the FDA's draft credibility framework and GMP validation both apply. ISPE's GAMP guide on AI translates this into practice for computerised systems, with emphasis on data, testing and change control.

reading.body:
AI used in pharmaceutical quality decisions now sits under two frameworks at once: the FDA's draft credibility guidance and existing GMP validation. ISPE's GAMP Guide on AI turns that overlap into practice for computerised systems, focused on data, testing and change control.

The pattern is that AI is being absorbed into the validation regime that already governs manufacturing software, not treated as a separate category. The FDA draft, issued in January 2025, reaches AI that supports quality decisions. The GAMP guide, published in 2025, addresses computerised systems generally, which is where most plant AI actually runs. The practical consequence is that a model influencing a batch or release decision inherits the same expectations as any validated system: documented data, documented testing, documented change control.

For AI specifically, this matters because the usual argument for a model is accuracy, and accuracy is not the standard here. A validated system is one whose behaviour is understood, bounded and reproducible, and a model that drifts or cannot explain a decision is hard to fit into that. The data also points to a consolidation benefit: one validation approach built on GAMP and the FDA framework can serve both US and EU inspections, so teams are not maintaining two evidentiary tracks.

What this does not cover is the substance of either document. No specific testing method, acceptance criterion, or data requirement is given, and the FDA text is a draft, so its final form is not settled. The dates and the two sources are all the record provides.
